source.author: Anastasia Kireeva
source.title: Low-degree hardness of finding the largest clique in Erdős–Rényi graph (problems 36-38)

methods.summary: Recast discounted high-degree energy as the analytic source-degree generating function G_h(z)=sum_k ||Pi_k h||_2^2 z^k, identified interior pressure Phi_r=log(1+G_h(e^{-2r})), and proved the sharp linear pressure-vs-damping budget limsup Phi_r/D < 2(alpha_t-r) for same-degree transfer.

Proved the exact softened two-copy identity 1+G_h(z)=E_{xi,xi'}<L_xi,z^N L_xi'> and showed how prior two-color polymer cancellation can certify interior rather than boundary pressure by weighting bichromatic clusters with z^{degree}; locality of that weighting remains an explicit model hypothesis outside diagonal/reference cases.

Built an exact nonproduct arity-two dimer-Gibbs null with long parity planting (bounded-arity latent XOR realization) for which source LDA through D_n is exactly zero, global Pi_2=Theta(n/D_n) is huge, discounted pressure Phi_r tends to zero for every fixed r>0, and natural single-site Gibbs heat-bath yields exact chi-square (1+q_t^{m_n})^{M_n}-1 -> 0 and hence TV convergence.

new_claims: Analytic source-degree generating-function formulation of discounted pressure and its exact interior-noise interpretation in degree-diagonal Markov cases.
Sharp same-degree analytic budget limsup Phi_r/D < 2(alpha_t-r), strictly broader than Phi_r=o(D).
Exact softened two-copy identity 1+G_h(z)=E<K_z> and a degree-weighted two-color polymer certification principle.
Explicit nonproduct dimer-Gibbs parity family separating volume-large global chi-square pressure from vanishing interior discounted pressure under natural single-site heat-bath.
Exact dimer noised collision formula chi2(P S_t||Q)=(1+q_t^m)^M-1 with q_t=((1+rho)e^{-2(1-rho)t}+(1-rho)e^{-2(1+rho)t})/2.
next_attack: Treat the interior degree generating function as a partition-function/analyticity object, break the independent-dimer/disjoint-parity symmetries to locate the first failure of small interior pressure, and derive a visible bounded-arity degree-weighted two-color KP certificate one local factor scale at a time.
